L45: # Quantitative Persistence and Regularity of Invariant Graphs for Dissipative Twist Maps
L46: Deyu Kong Address: School of Mathematics and Statistics, Beijing Institute of Technology, Beijing 100081, China Email address: dykong@bit.edu.cn , Jessica Elisa Massetti Address: Department of Mathematics, University of Rome Tor Vergata, Via della ricerca scientifica 1, 00133 Rome, Italy Email address: massetti@axp.mat.uniroma2.it and Lin Wang Address: School of Mathematics and Statistics, Beijing Institute of Technology, Beijing 100081, China Email address: lwang@bit.edu.cn
L47: ###### Abstract.
L48: In this paper we study the robustness of invariant Lagrangian graphs for dissipative twist maps on $\mathbb{T}^{d}\times\mathbb{R}^{d}$ in the $C^{r}$ category, for any $r\geq 1$, and show their persistence as invariant global attractors under quantitative sharp conditions involving both the size of dissipation parameter and the perturbation at stake. Note that when $d>1$ the geometric Lagrangian property of the invariant manifold may be destroyed, so that the graph may persist but fail to be Lagrangian.
L49: In general, additional dynamical requirements on the twist maps come into play if we intend to preserve also the Lagrangian property. In this line, we first study their persistence for general perturbations, then we restrict to the class of exact conformally symplectic twist maps and provide quantitative sharp conditions for the persistence of invariant exact Lagrangian graphs, without assuming any condition on the tangential dynamics of the manifold.
L50: The persistence result relies on a combination of a suitable multidimensional Herman–Mather formula proved in this setting and contraction estimates that provide sharp bounds on the $C^{1}$-norm of the perturbation to get a unique, globally attracting $C^{r}$ graph. In dimension $d=1$, by further assuming that that the circle map induced by the graph has irrational rotation number, we prove that every $C^{1}$ invariant graph of a $C^{k}$ map is $C^{k}$ for $k=2,3,\ldots,\infty$.

L152: ### 1.3. Regularity in dimension one
L153: The upper bounds $\eta_{r}(\lambda)$ introduced above tend to zero as $r\to\infty$, so they do not give $C^{\infty}$ regularity for a fixed nonzero perturbation. In dimension one, the rotation number is somehow related to the regularity and can be used to derive information about. The conservative theory of invariant curves was developed by Herman, Salamon, and Katznelson–Ornstein [【45†Her83】, 【61†Her86】, 【62†Sal04】, 【63†KO95】].
L154: For dissipative maps, we ask whether irrational rotation number allows an invariant graph to inherit the regularity of the ambient map, and what regularity must initially be assumed of the graph. Hall’s smooth annulus maps with attracting Lipschitz circles carrying Denjoy dynamics [【64†Hall83】] also motivate the latter question.
